properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 15 at 8:56AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Thursday was 2.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage near 2.7 feet through late week. A rise near Moderate
Flood Stage is forecast into early next week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EDT.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 15 at 7:49AM CDT until October 15 at 10:45AM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
FFWOUN

The National Weather Service in Norman has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Wichita County in northern Texas...

* Until 1045 AM CDT.

* At 749 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Wichita Falls, Sheppard AFB, Pleasant Valley and Cashion.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Wind Advisory, northeast winds 20 to 30 mph with
gusts 35 to 55 mph expected. Strongest winds will be near the
foothills of the Santa Ana mountains, with gusts up to 70 mph
possible. For the Heat Advisory, temperatures up to 95 expected.

* WHERE...Orange County Inland Areas.

* WHEN...For the Wind Advisory, until noon PDT Saturday. For the Heat
Advisory, from 10 AM this morning to 8 PM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Oklahoma, including the following
county, Hughes.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

flooded.

through Thursday morning. Storms will include very heavy rainfall
rates. Widespread additional rainfall amounts of 0.5-1 inches are
likely, and a few locations will see additional rainfall of up 3
inches.

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

through Thursday morning. Storms will include very heavy rainfall
rates. Widespread additional rainfall amounts of 0.5-1 inches are
likely, and a few locations will see additional rainfall of up 3
inches.

properties.instruction:

to take action should flooding develop.
